A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BACO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including the image-based annotation interfaces. Substantial reorganization does not prevent matching retained content.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments on NoveltyBench, WildChat, and Narrative-Discourse, router and model-pair comparisons, and human evaluations of quality, diversity, and creativity.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds verifiable-task evaluations, multi-turn dialogue results, repetition-distribution measurements, and runtime and memory comparisons.

M1.justification: The token-level collaboration framework, routing strategies, word-boundary switching, aligned first token, and aligned-controlled termination are retained. Algorithm 1 in v2 documents rules already described in v1 Section 3 and Appendix A; it does not establish a changed decoding procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains the three original open-ended datasets and adds GSM8K mathematical reasoning, IFEval verifiable instruction constraints, MT-Bench multi-turn dialogue, and Artificial Hivemind chat queries. Mathematical correctness, explicit constraint satisfaction, and multi-turn interaction substantially expand the evaluated task requirements.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator sets are retained. v2 adds Min-p to the Artificial Hivemind comparison alongside Top-p, and evaluates Back Translation, Mix-of-Agents, and Multi-Agent Debate in the new runtime comparison. These are localized comparator additions, not replacements of the main comparisons.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce GSM8K accuracy and Pass@10, IFEval strict/loose prompt- and instruction-level accuracy, and a Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct repetition test with BACO's threshold chosen to match Min-p quality. Runtime comparisons use a common A100 80 GB and HuggingFace implementation. These add substantial evaluation designs without establishing changes to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds a repetition-distribution analysis examining low-similarity generations and a runtime, throughput, and memory analysis examining computational cost. The original router and model-pair ablations, switching-pattern analyses, early-stopping examples, and threshold case study remain unchanged after relocation.

E5.justification: The new runtime Table A6 introduces plus/minus reporting, such as BACO's 22.9 ± 4.5 seconds per sample. Neither the meaning of the dispersion term nor a repetition count is specified, so additional runs cannot be inferred. The retained experiments do not gain seed counts or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Original main performance tables and appendix Tables A7-A11 retain their values. New results include GSM8K/IFEval trade-off curves, MT-Bench Coverage of 0.681 versus 0.320, and runtime measurements. Figure 5 reports 15% low-similarity generations for BACO versus 8% for Min-p at nearly matched rewards, 8.083 versus 8.079. Format/content agreement values of 0.166 and 0.244 are omitted from the retained human study.

T1.justification: The collaboration equations, diversity definitions, normalization, Coverage and Dominance formulas, and narrative-diversity calculations are retained. The added pseudocode formalizes existing operational rules; no new theorem, proof, substantive mathematical assumption, or revised derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims remain controllable diversity-quality improvement through inference-time base-aligned collaboration, a family of lightweight routers, and validation across diversity-quality spaces. Both abstracts retain the headline 21.3% improvement and human-evaluation support. Additional benchmarks strengthen support without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the optimistic efficiency discussion with approximately two forward passes in the worst case and explicit prototype overhead. It adds reasons for excluding learned routers and clearer scope limitations. The creativity discussion becomes preliminary and drops the earlier explanation of conflicting literature, while the principal switching and early-stopping interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds decoding pseudocode, explicitly discloses no top-k truncation and Diverse Beam Search settings of 20 beams, 10 groups, and penalty 1.0, and specifies hardware/software for timing. These are documentation additions, not demonstrated changes to earlier settings. Existing code/data links remain, with a project-page link added.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the new benchmarks, Min-p comparison, and efficiency discussion, while removing parts of the creativity debate, including citations to Si et al. and Gupta and Pruthi. The related-work discussion is largely retained, and BACO's positioning against quality-focused token collaboration remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially condenses and rewrites the introduction, method explanation, results, and discussion. Related work moves from Section 7 to Appendix A; creativity discussion joins human evaluation; narrative evaluation details receive a separate appendix. It also adds a limitations section and removes the standalone reproducibility and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of figures and tables. v2 adds verifiable-task plots, a repetition heatmap, and a runtime table. Existing discourse plots, contribution plots, and annotation screenshots are retained and repositioned rather than removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence that diversity gains can coexist with verifiable correctness through GSM8K and IFEval, beyond v1's open-ended quality assessments. Table A6 also replaces qualitative efficiency assurances with measured latency, throughput, and memory costs, making practical trade-offs assessable. Pseudocode improves implementation clarity. Some new protocols remain underspecified and two human-agreement statistics are lost, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the stronger validation and cost transparency.
